messages.subject: Infinite value after imputation
messages.body_plain:
Dear MSstats team:

I got two questions about the imputation.

1. After imputation (data.name.TMP <- dataProcess (raw = data.name <http://data.name>, fillIncompleteRows = TRUE, normalization = "equalizeMedians", summaryMethod = "TMP", censoredInt = "NA", cutoffCensored = "minFeature", MBimpute= TRUE), I think I am doing the right thing?

However, after exported the tablet to excel, I found some proteins has the Log2FC label of "inf" and MissingPercentage >0.5. I know this is because the intensity is missing in one condition.
The question is, I thought with imputation, a value should be give to those "0" intensity, so a proper pvalue or FDR and FC can be performed?

2. If this is what it is, is it valid to use these proteins as our targets, saying with MissingPercentage<0.5, with infinity log2FC value? Can they still be considered as found in one condition, while not in the other OR they can only be used as outliers?

Thanks a lot for your help and look forward your reply.
Best
Cheng

messages.subject: Re: Infinite value after imputation
messages.body_plain:
Dear Cheng,

We only impute missing values in a run if we observed at least one feature in that run. If the protein was not at all found in a run we leave the intensities in that run missing. When the protein is present in one condition but completely absent in all the runs in another condition, formal statistical inference cannot be performed. In these cases we set log2FC to infinity, and p-value to 0 without performing the tests. This is to avoid losing the proteins that can be biologically meaningful. So yes, you can use these proteins as targets for follow-up, as long as you can reliably identify them in at least one condition.

HTH
Olga

messages.subject: [Installation] MSstats v3.6 in Bioconductor v3.4
messages.body_plain:
Dear MSstats users,

In Bioconductor v3.4 (from November 2016), MSstats v3.6 is released.
We just found that there are some installation issue for this new version. The installation from Bioconductor should be followed.

1. Run below.
source("https://bioconductor.org/biocLite.R")

Then, you should see
Bioconductor version 3.4 (BiocInstaller 1.24.0), ?biocLite for help

If you see, 'Bioconductor version 3.3', the older version of MSstats, v3.4 or v3.3.12 will be installed. Then Run below, it will upgrade the bioconductor version

biocLite("BiocUpgrade")

Then, check again, whether it says Bioconduction version 3.4 or not.

source("https://bioconductor.org/biocLite.R")

2. Install MSstats. All related packages will be installed.

biocLite("MSstats")

3. load MSstats and check MSstats version.
library(MSstats)
?MSstats

Please check the help file says MSstats version 3.6 (or v 3.5.6 also fine) or not.

messages.subject: [FAQ] different result before and after v3.5.6
messages.subject_clean: [FAQ] different result before and after v3.5.6
messages.body_plain:
Dear MSstats users,

Please check the detailed updates in 'Changes since the previous version' pdf files from MSstats home page or 'MSstats' page of msstats.org <http://msstats.org>

After v3.5.6 of MSstats, one of the significant update is that MSstats applies the algorithm for deciding the data-specific censoring threshold. Then, inference result (result of groupComparison) can be different that previous version. The related option is maxQuantileforCensored=0.999 in dataProcess function. and now you can see which measurements are censored in profile plots. (empty dots) If you don't want to apply it, please use maxQuantileforCensored=NULL. Then the result will be the same with the result from v3.2.

- Meena

messages.subject: DIA/SWATH - quantification, normalisation and multi-level comparison (disease state and genotype together)
messages.subject_clean: DIA/SWATH - quantification, normalisation and multi-level comparison (disease state and genotype together)
messages.body_plain:
Hi Meena and Olga,

I've started using MSStats (V.3.5.6) to analyse my DIA/SWATH data (25 healthy, 25 disease - 3 injection replicates).
I used a blocking during sample prep and runs - as I learned from Olga on last year's proteomics course.

Questions:
Does MSStats automatically use fragments only when summing intensities or will precursors get included if present in MSStatsInput.csv? My Skyline MSStatsInput shows fragments and precursors (because I've chosen to show precursors in skyline) but I'm pretty sure that DIA analysis should be carried out using fragments only.
With regard to my experiment, how do I best normalize? Is median normalization ok in label-free DIA data? I have some heavy SIS peptides spiked-in that I could potentially use.
I would like to compare healthy and disease (2 conditions) and on top of that compare a specific influence of genotype (3 conditions - GG, GC, CC) within Healthy and Disease. Can I do this in MSStats.

Please let me know if you need further detail or files made available.

Regards

messages.subject_clean: DIA/SWATH - quantification, normalisation and multi-level comparison (disease state and genotype together)
messages.body_plain:
Please see below:

1. MSstats uses fragments for summarization.

2. It should be okay, and you may want to cross check the normalization results with both options. It's usually a good idea to check the profile plots (before and after normalization) of some proteins that you know well.

3. It's possible - you'll need to provide the genotype in the Condition column, and specify the comparisons you'd like to make by defining the contrast matrix (see 4.1.6 of the document at http://msstats.org/wp-content/uploads/2016/11/MSstats_v3.6_manual.pdf)

HTH
Tsung-Heng
